Disney said Direct-to-Consumer operating results increased $2,639 million, to operating income of $143 million from an operating loss of $2,496 million, "due to improved results at Disney+." The filing points to higher subscription fees and advertising revenue. It also points to lower non-sports programming costs at Disney+, partly offset by cricket programming costs at Disney+ Hotstar.
Disney reported that Direct-to-Consumer operating results increased $2,639 million, to operating income of $143 million from an operating loss of $2,496 million, and attributed this to improved results at Disney+.
On revenue, Disney said subscription fee growth reflected a 10% increase from higher effective rates due to retail pricing increases and 6% from subscriber growth. A 2% unfavorable foreign exchange impact partly offset this.
Disney said higher advertising revenue reflected a 26% increase from higher impressions, partly offset by a 12% decrease from lower rates.
On costs, Disney said the decrease in programming and production costs at Disney+ and other was attributable to lower costs for non-sports content on Disney+. Higher cricket programming costs at Disney+ Hotstar partly offset this.
Selling, general, administrative and other costs rose $406 million, to $4,574 million from $4,168 million. Disney attributed this primarily to increases in marketing and labor costs, which partly offset the improvement.
